one_liner: Intercom has a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 for public apps, a free developer workspace with access tokens, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for public apps accessing other people's data, set up self-serve in the Developer Hub. Access tokens are for private apps on your own workspace. OAuth tokens don't expire.
access_notes: A free developer workspace (US region only) gives an app, an access token and OAuth setup. It has some limitations versus a paid workspace. Third-party sources conflict on whether the API needs a paid plan for real workspaces. Nango confirms the free dev account and test workspace work. App review is only needed to publish to the Intercom App Store.
blocker_notes: The free developer workspace gives working credentials. Customers need their own Intercom plan. App review applies only to marketplace listing.

evidence.quote: OAuth is for if you're building a public app that accesses other people's Intercom data.
We provide you with an Access Token as soon as you create an app on your workspace.
If you are building a public integration that will have access to other peoples' Intercom data you are required to set up OAuth.
Developer workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only.
Free, self-signup for an Intercom Developer account.
Only required for apps published to the Intercom App Store.
